title: Go back to the previous build after an upgrade that succeeded, and one build stamp for every binary
purpose: DIRECTORY-045 upgrades a running install and returns to the previous build only when the upgrade itself fails. A build that starts ready and misbehaves an hour later has no way back but hand moves in the install folder, which an ordinary person cannot make. Its build stamp is also four byte-identical build.rs files that a test holds equal: one script copied four times, not one script. Amended 28 September 2026 21:05 by Waffles after Archie's read against the tree.
task: Add `lys identity upgrade --back`, which returns the install to the build kept beside it through the same stop, swap, start and ready path as an upgrade; and move the build stamp into one build-support crate that each binary's build.rs calls.

requirements.title: `lys identity upgrade --back`
requirements.spec: Behavioural. `lys identity upgrade --back` (the same verb, so there is one path) reads the version of every binary in bin/ and in bin.previous/ before stopping anything, and refuses by name when there is no bin.previous/ (nothing_to_return_to) or a version cannot be read. It then stops the broker and the service through their exit locks, exchanges bin/ with bin.previous/, the configuration and compose files with config.previous/ (DIRECTORY-045 R5) and surface/ with surface.previous/ when that exists, recreating any compose service whose definition changes (so the build it leaves becomes the one kept, and --back again returns to it), starts both and waits on their readiness events, and writes install/build.json. A failure on the way puts back what it moved, exactly as an upgrade does, and names the binary and its log. It never writes data/ or a credential, and it reads and honours an unfinished upgrade's intent record first (DIRECTORY-045 R7). The Build line on the account screen shows the build now running. Each build records the newest data format it writes (the log event kinds it can read, as a format number in install/build.json and its --version detail). Before stopping anything, --back compares the kept build's format with the data's, and when the older build cannot read the data it refuses back_would_not_read, naming the first event kind the older build does not know. Data is never rolled back.
acceptance: After an upgrade that succeeded, --back leaves the earlier commit running, answering /api/authority with that build, and --back again returns to the newer one.
With no bin.previous/ it is refused nothing_to_return_to and nothing is stopped.
A start failure during --back leaves the build it began from running and names the binary and its log.
After an upgrade whose build writes a new event kind, --back is refused back_would_not_read naming that kind, and nothing is stopped.

files_changed.note: `stated()` (line 203) reads the commit from the first --version line and the `data format N adds KIND, KIND` lines after it. BASELINE_FORMAT (line 186) is 1, used for a build that states no format. BuildRecord.data_format (line 259) is the format high-water written to install/build.json, and recorded_format() (line 333) reads it back. The stop/swap/start/ready/put-back flow moved into `cycle()` (line 491), which upgrade and back share. run() (line 545) chooses --from or --back. The module doc states the new invariants, and the file declares `mod back` and the back_tests module.

`back()` (line 101) runs --back. It refuses an intent record (refuse_unfinished, line 27), a missing kept build (nothing_to_return_to, line 112), an unreadable version, a data format the kept build cannot read (check_formats, line 71, back_would_not_read naming the first unknown event kind), and a leftover `*.exchanging` folder (aside, line 43). All of these are checked before any stop. It then exchanges bin/ and surface/ with their kept folders (exchange, line 59) through the shared cycle (line 153).

Upgrade now flattens a `Source` struct (line 82): a clap group requiring exactly one of `--from DIR` or `--back`. `--surface` conflicts with `--back` (line 62). main.rs is unchanged because the variant still has the fields `from`, `surface` and `root`.
New kinds NothingToReturnTo, BackWouldNotRead and UpgradeUnfinished, named nothing_to_return_to, back_would_not_read and upgrade_unfinished.

Scratch-root tests with stub binaries. They cover: back and back again; refusal with nothing kept; a start failure during back; the back_would_not_read refusal plus a control case where it passes; the format high-water; intent-record and exchange refusals; parsing of the data-format detail; CLI group parsing; and the new error names.

dev.how: Acceptance row 1 (after a successful upgrade, --back runs the earlier commit, and --back again returns to the newer one) is met. Evidence: upgrade_back_tests.rs:253 back_runs_the_kept_build_and_back_again_runs_the_newer. It upgrades A→B, and after --back the running processes report A, bin/ answers A, bin.previous/ answers B, the screens are A, and build.json records A. A second --back brings B back. data/, identity.json and deployment.toml stay byte-identical throughout. /api/authority answers the running binary's own stamp (lys-identity-server/src/read_api.rs:43, tested by lys-identity-server/tests/authority_build.rs), so the test shows the kept binary running rather than reading /api/authority directly. The scratch-install verification step reads it live. Acceptance row 2 is met: :287 is refused NothingToReturnTo, the pid files are unchanged, A is still running, and no bin.previous/ is created. Acceptance row 3 is met: :302 makes the kept service exit before ready. The error is upgrade_failed, naming `lys-identity-server did not start ready` and its log path, and saying 'the build it began from is back and running'. B is running again, and A is still the kept build. Acceptance row 4 is met: :330 upgrades to a build that states `data format 2 adds team.renamed`. --back is then refused back_would_not_read naming `team.renamed`, with pids unchanged. A control case gives the same kept commit knowledge of format 2, and --back then runs, which proves the refusal comes from the format alone. :357 shows the format high-water survives a later build that states no format. :376 shows install/upgrade.json refuses both --back and --from, and a leftover bin.exchanging refuses --back, all before anything stops. The Build line on the account screen reads /api/authority from the running server, so after --back it shows the build now running with no surface change. Nothing writes data/ or a credential.
dev.deviation: 1) The file wall was not held to. upgrade.rs would have reached 541 code lines against the 500 limit, so the --back logic went into a new submodule, crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/back.rs. This follows DIRECTORY-045 R7's plan to split upgrade.rs into upgrade/ modules. CN9 asks for review before a file outside the wall is edited; this one was created to keep the file-length gate passing and is named here for the reviewer. 2) The real binaries do not yet state a data format. The format is read from `data format N adds KIND` lines in a binary's --version detail, and producing those lines in lys-identity-server needs crates/lys-identity-server/src/main.rs and its tests/version.rs, which are outside this brief's files (CN9). Until a revision adds them, every real build reads as format 1, so --back is never refused back_would_not_read in production. The mechanism is fully tested with stub builds. 3) DIRECTORY-045 R5 (config.previous/ and compose re-render) and R7 (the intent record's format and finishing) are not on this branch; only the brief text was amended in ead3685. So --back exchanges bin/ and surface/ only. It honours an intent record by refusing by name (upgrade_unfinished) whenever install/upgrade.json exists, on both --back and --from, and does not finish or put back that upgrade. 4) The failure line printed by the shared cycle still begins `upgrade failed:` under --back.

checklist.note: --back stops the processes, exchanges the folders, starts them and waits for ready through the same cycle as an upgrade, and records build.json. The config.previous/ exchange and full intent-record recovery wait on DIRECTORY-045 R5 and R7 (see deviation).

stories.note: One command, `lys identity upgrade --back`, returns to the kept build after an upgrade that started fine. It is refused by name when that is impossible or unsafe.

requirements.title: One build stamp
requirements.spec: Structural. A build-support crate, crates/lys-build-stamp, holds the one function that computes the stamp (head commit, `; dirty`, or `not built from a git commit`) and the rerun-if lines. Each of lys, lys-identity-server, lys-secrets and lys-home lists it under build-dependencies and its build.rs is one call. The byte-identity test is removed with the copies; the stamp's own tests (exported tree, fresh commit, dirty) move into the crate and run against it.
acceptance: No two build.rs files in the workspace hold the stamp logic; each is one call.
The crate's tests prove the three stamp forms.
Every binary's --version still prints its name, version and commit.

files_changed.note: The build-support crate. Standard library only; tempfile is a dev-dependency.

The one stamp. stamp() (line 51) gives the head commit, `; dirty`, or NO_COMMIT (line 21). cargo_lines() (line 87) gives the rerun-if-changed and LYS_BUILD lines. emit() (line 98) is the whole of each build.rs.

Checks that each of the four build.rs files is exactly `fn main() { lys_build_stamp::emit(); }` and that each Cargo.toml lists the crate under build-dependencies. Builds a probe crate through lys's build.rs from an exported tree, a fresh commit, and a dirty tree. Also checks the cargo lines.
Adds crates/lys-build-stamp as a member and a workspace dependency.
Adds the lys-build-stamp package and lists it as a dependency of lys, lys-identity-server, lys-secrets and lys-home. Needed by the new crate; not in the brief's file list.
The byte-identity test and the probe tests are removed; the probe tests moved to the stamp crate. The --version/-V test stays.

dev.how: Acceptance row 1 (no two build.rs files hold the stamp logic; each is one call) is met. The four build.rs files are a doc comment plus `fn main() { lys_build_stamp::emit(); }`, and stamp.rs:37 asserts this for each of them, along with the build-dependencies entry, counting four crates checked. Acceptance row 2 (the crate's tests prove the three stamp forms) is met. stamp.rs:91 shows an exported tree says `not built from a git commit`. stamp.rs:100 shows a clean build of a fresh commit gives its 40-character commit, and after a change it gives `COMMIT; dirty`. Both build a probe crate whose build.rs is lys's own one-call file, depending on lys-build-stamp. Acceptance row 3 (every binary's --version still prints its name, version and commit) is met. The main.rs files are unchanged and still print `NAME VERSION (LYS_BUILD)`. The existing version tests check this: crates/lys/tests/version.rs, crates/lys-identity-server/tests/version.rs, crates/lys-secrets/tests/version.rs and crates/lys-home/tests/version.rs.
dev.deviation: Cargo.lock was edited by hand to add the new path crate, because no cargo command was to be run. The brief's file list does not name it, but a new workspace crate requires it.

checklist.note: One shared crate computes the stamp; no build.rs is copied.

stories.note: Each binary still names its build, which is what --back reads to name the build it returns to.

boundaries: SHALL NOT change what an upgrade writes beyond bin/, bin.previous/, the configuration and compose files and config.previous/, the screens, the logs, the process files, install/upgrade.json and install/build.json; data is never rolled back.
SHALL NOT add a timeout, deadline, poll, #[allow], #[ignore] or any bypass.
SHALL NOT add a silent fallback: every failure is a named refusal.
verification: The full Lys gate, ast-grep scan and surface checks exit 0 at the card's head, measured by the card round.
On a scratch install: upgrade to a newer build, --back, and read the older commit from /api/authority; --back again and read the newer one.
